text:
eli_acme: hey, embedding endpoint suddenly started returning 768-d vectors for our prod model (we expect 1536). started after we switched to the int8 quant profile. getting downstream failures in our similarity service.

maya_support: thanks for reporting — can you paste the exact API call you used and the model name you passed? quick question: did you switch model variant as well or only the precision/quant flag?

eli_acme: curl i used: 
```
curl https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{\"model\":\"embed-large-v2\",\"input\":\"welcome to our app\",\"quantization\":\"int8\"}'
```
We thought setting quantization=int8 would just change compute/size, not dims. no other model param changed.

maya_support: hmm, thanks. quick sanity check: can you run the same request but remove the quantization flag (or set quantization: fp16) and paste the vector length? also can you include the raw JSON response you get?

eli_acme: with no quantization i get vector length 1536. with quantization=int8 i get 768. response snippet: `{\"data\":[{\"embedding\":[0.001, 0.002, ... total 768 values] }] }`. error from our service: `ValueError: expected 1536, got 768` when feeding into faiss index.

maya_support: appreciate the repro. two quick possibilities: 1) you're accidentally hitting a different model variant (e.g., embed-large-v2-compact) that has half dims, or 2) there's a bug in the quantization pipeline that strips half of the vector before packaging. also need to confirm whether your client is decompressing/decoding correctly (some clients pack int8 raw bytes).

eli_acme: we double-checked model name in our code path — it's dynamically set from config and reads `embed-large-v2` (not compact). and we receive JSON numbers, not raw bytes.

maya_support: ok. i'm going to ask eng-ml to look at the quantization rollout metadata. @raj_engineering can you take a look at model-registry mappings and the int8 build for embed-large-v2?

raj_engineering: pinged. quick note: int8 quantization should never change embedding dimensionality. the quant profile only changes numeric precision and weight packing. potential causes: an intermediate pooling op that changed (e.g., using a different pooling head for a quant build) or a buggy serializer that treats int8 payload as half-length array. i'll pull the logs for the quant build.

deploy_bot: deploy started: model-embed-large-v2-int8 - rollout batch 2 -> prod (id: dpl-2026-03-15-42)

eli_acme: timeline: we enabled quantization on 2026-03-15 10:12 UTC and started seeing errors at 10:15. looks correlated with your rollout.

maya_support: that rollout info helps. i'm escalating to oncall because this is causing production errors for the customer. @anna_oncall can you triage and consider rollback?

anna_oncall: looking now. initial triage: traffic shows requests routed to worker pool `emb-v2-int8-prod`. i'm pausing further rollouts and spinning up a fallback pool using `embed-large-v2-fp16` to handle this tenant's traffic.

raj_engineering: digging into logs for dpl-2026-03-15-42. found this in serializer service (emb-serialize): `WARN: serialization: detected payload_type=int8_bytes, converting -> packed_floats length/2` — looks like serializer attempted to reinterpret an int8-packed buffer as if it was half-precision floats, then emitted halves. potential bug in serializer that converts int8 bytes to float list by pairwise casting.

maya_support: that would explain half-length array. @raj_engineering can you confirm whether the model runtime is returning float arrays or raw packed int8?

raj_engineering: model runtime returns raw int8 bytes when quantization=int8 to save network bandwidth for high-throughput workloads. normally emb-serialize unpacks into float32 vectors on the control plane. appears the unpacker has an edge-case when a 'quant_profile' header equals 'int8:fast' — it's using a different codepath that currently wrongfully splits the buffer.

eli_acme: so is the correct mitigation to ask you to rollback the int8 rollout? we can't change our service to handle 768 dims.

anna_oncall: rolling back the problematic rollout for all customers now. priority: restore compatibility. ETA ~4m for gradual rollback.

maya_support: Meanwhile, as a workaround you can pin your requests to `model: embed-large-v2-fp16` to avoid hitting the int8 pool until this is fixed. also we can enable a tenant-level routing rule to keep your traffic on fp16. want me to do that?

eli_acme: yes please apply tenant routing rule. also would like a postmortem on root cause and whether any customers saw silent dim truncation (we want to know if any vectors were silently re-ingested into indices).

raj_engineering: notes for postmortem: bug in emb-serialize int8-unpacker codepath introduced during optimization commit `opt/serialize-int8-2026-03-14`. root cause: incorrect byte-to-float decoding routine assumed little-endian pairwise aggregation. fix: revert to tested unpacker and add roundtrip tests that assert identical dims and numeric shape across quant profiles. adding unit test and integration test for `quantization=int8` returning float arrays of same length.

maya_support: for support ticket closure steps: 1) rollback completed? 2) tenant routing pinned to fp16 for eli_acme 3) reproduce case and collect logs + correlation id 4) engineering PR to fix unpacker + tests 5) postmortem and customer notification.

deploy_bot: rollback complete: dpl-2026-03-15-42 -> rollback success (duration 180s)

anna_oncall: rollback finished, traffic back to fp16 pools. @maya_support please confirm eli_acme can re-run their failing job.

eli_acme: re-ran the same request (quantization=int8) against the endpoint now and it returns 1536-length vectors (seems routed to fp16 pool). thanks for fast action. can you confirm whether our previously generated 768-d vectors are safe to drop?

raj_engineering: short answer: yes drop. those were truncated outputs from our serializer bug — they are invalid for FAISS ingestion. for safety we recommend re-embedding the affected documents. we'll provide a list of impacted time ranges and potential IDs.

maya_support: i'm creating a follow-up ticket to coordinate re-ingestion + any compensation for reprocessing costs. also we'll add a note to the status page and follow up with a detailed postmortem.

eli_acme: appreciated. one other ask: can you add an API flag that forces response vectors to be returned as float32 JSON (no packing) even for quantized models? that would have made debugging simpler.

raj_engineering: good suggestion — we already have an internal header X-Embeddings-Format: float32/raw that will be promoted to public API. will track in the postmortem.

maya_support: closing loop: rollback done, tenant pinned to fp16, eng will ship fix + tests, postmortem coming. assigning follow-ups: ENG-1427 (fix unpacker), SPT-768 (tenant re-ingest coordination), DOCS-99 (publicize X-Embeddings-Format).

eli_acme: thanks all. appreciate the quick turnaround and the clear next steps. :thumbsup:

maya_support: glad we could help — will DM you the re-ingest window and invoice/credits details once we have scoped work. :wave:
